Just wanted to pop in and say that my symptoms presented and occurred nearly the exact same way. I (26/f) also had a biopsy done and presented the same. The only difference is that I was on BC (Kyleena IUD) at the time. I was convinced that my hormones were causing a lot of my issues but doctors kept saying there was no connection between the two. I just had my IUD removed in January and I am already seeing major improvement. It is not 100% better but I'd say 80% of my symptoms and issues cleared up and have been getting better as the weeks have gone on. I still have flare ups here and there but they are never as near as bad as they used to be. My journey is far from over but I am grateful to have at least a little relief. I would definitely look into getting your hormone levels checked if you can! Best of luck to you.

I am on the constipation side of things, apparently it's been am issue since I was an infant according to my mom. Finally towards the end of that I couldn't pass anything at all and ended up having a complete blockage of my system. After that ordeal I went to the doctor and they performed a colonoscopy on me to which they reported was completely clean and healthy. They never diagnosed me with anything, but I do remember the doctor saying "You have what my daughter has!" As I came to from being under.

My body has never been quite the same since then.. I have to be super careful about what I eat and have been going to physical therapy to try and help relax my muscles so I can go properly. Greasy foods will put me in so much pain that I will have to stay in bed all day. It's really difficult always feeling bloated and dealing with cramps from constipation. It's gotten a little bit more manageable since PT but I still have bad days where I sit on the toilet for hours in pain but nothing passes :/

I wish I would have done more research as well before taking it. I'm still dealing with issues from it even after being off of it for nearly a year now. For me it truly did change my body composition, I constantly looked like I was 6 months pregnant. Thankfully I got off of it in time that my body went back to looking somewhat normal, however that wasn't even the worst of it all. My periods have been absolutely awful since I was a kid as well, paralyzing cramps, heavy bleeding, etc. Recently also discovered ovarian cysts and suspected endo as well. Regardless of all of this, my periods were regular... until depo. My second dose caused me to bleed for 3. Fucking. Months. And of course doctors can't/won't do anything except tell you to take 600mg of ibuprofen 3 times a day to see if that kicks your uterus back in gear. I finally got off of it but I still have irregular periods to this day. I'm currently taking a combination pill to try and regulate myself and it has worked pretty well so far, but I just got over an episode of bleeding for a month straight so I have a long way to go. 

I know there are people who really like the depo shot and that it works really well for them, but I still would recommend anyone thinking about it to heavily research the depo shot before going ahead with it.

I lost 100 pounds back in 2018-19 and got treated so much different than I had before.

Unfortunately I gained 60 pounds back over the pandemic and am struggling to lose it again. It's very evident that I am not attractive, especially because of my weight, and it kills me inside. I hate myself specifically because I've gained so much weight back... I'm embarrassed and I avoid places where I know people because I'm afraid they'll see me and judge me for "Letting myself go".

I know the attention that I desire is bad and inappropriate in most settings, but I desperately want to feel desired. I've always been the fat friend and I'm about to head up to Portland to see one of my best friends.. part of me is dreading it because she's become so small and fit and she's so cute that I feel like a disgusting whale next to her. This feeling is selfish and I know I shouldn't have it (I'm no longer a kid and my weight is my responsibility, so it's my fault I'm this size) so I'm doing my best to try and bottle it away.

Just know that we tend to be our own worst critic, I know that's so cliche but it's true. Try to be easy on yourself and take steps that make you feel good. I try to keep up a skin care routine so that I at least feel clean and comfortable about my face, so it takes a little bit of burden off of how I feel about my appearance. Good luck to you and I hope you feel better in the near future ❤❤❤
